findings.summary: The residual contour call passes no linestyles, so matplotlib applies its default negative-contour dash: negative residual levels render dashed and positive levels solid, and the legend keys only one solid blue 'residual' swatch (render.py:175). A reader therefore cannot tell a positive residual from a negative one, which is the quantity the record itself reports sign-first (frame-137 sup +224.73 mWb, frame-179 sup -127.30 mWb, and the sign differs between the two cases). The damage is worse than an absent key: in the boundary-band panel the region mask already breaks every contour into fragments, so 'dash means negative level' and 'gap means the contour left the band' look identical. Applies to all three figures. Verified rather than inferred: a contour of a bipolar field with these levels, drawn with this call's arguments under the same matplotlib 3.11.1, renders the three negative levels with a dash gap and the three positive levels continuous at the same scan row (positive-control pixels read 3 at both scan positions, negative read 3 then 0).

The residual level set is rescaled to each case's own max |r| (render.py:86-88) and drawn at one weight (render.py:119-127), so a 3.3e-16 Wb roundoff field receives exactly the treatment given to a 0.22 Wb physical residual. In the outside-plasma panel this produces roughly fifty nested loops and short segments that outweigh the solved-flux contours, and a reader moving between the three figures sees comparable residual structure where the magnitudes differ by fifteen orders. The caption does state that these contours are roundoff, so the reading is recoverable, but the picture's visual weight contradicts the caption.

Two distinct objects share the single legend entry 'EFIT flux / boundary': the 0.75 pt dashed EFIT flux contours (render.py:99-108) and the 1.8 pt dashed EFIT boundary polygon (render.py:139-146), which are different features at different weights. Separately, the grey reference null set is drawn (render.py:148-155) but the legend keyed for hollow marks is a triangle only ('EFIT nulls', render.py:195-203), leaving the grey reference cross in the lower left of each panel unkeyed. A reader can see these marks and cannot identify them.

The filled red solved-axis triangle and the hollow grey EFIT-null triangle abut in the boundary-band and outside-plasma panels, so the two glyphs merge into one mark and the reader cannot see whether the solved axis and the reference axis actually differ. Neither the caption nor the legend separates them. The renderer's text guard (render_panels.py:435, called at render.py:32) checks text artists against the canvas and against each other only, and render.py:34-37 checks text against the axes box, so no guard covers marker-against-marker collisions.

The axes limits are set to the data extent and the spines are removed by the house style, so residual contours that reach the edge of the grid stop in mid-air with nothing to say so. In the outside-plasma panels of all three figures the outermost blue contour ends against blank space, which reads as a truncated line rather than as a contour leaving the domain; the same is true of the outer grey flux contours.

notes: Read-only review. No file outside the two declared record paths was written, and no figure, caption or script was edited. Judged only from the three named PNGs; no SVG was opened, read or rendered, and the figure-to-path mapping was established from the fragment's regional decomposition tables, not from the images' own filenames. The one instrument check run was a bare matplotlib contour of a bipolar synthetic field in a scratch directory, with the positive levels as its positive control; it produced no image file and wrote nothing into the repository.
